title: Set of open substacks and their unions under scheme pullback
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, meaning a stack in groupoids on $S$-schemes with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Stacks and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], smooth uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and universes use [def-weil-size-convention]. An open substack is a strictly full substack whose pullback by every scheme is an open subscheme. Open substacks of $\mathcal X$, up to equivalence over $\mathcal X$, admit a set of representatives. For every set $I$ and family of open substacks $(\mathcal X_i\subseteq\mathcal X)_{i\in I}$ there is an algebraic open substack $\mathcal W=\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal X_i\subseteq\mathcal X$, containing every $\mathcal X_i$ and contained in every open substack containing them all. For every scheme $T$ and map $T\to\mathcal X$, if $T_i=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_i$ is the corresponding open subscheme of $T$, then $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$ is the open subscheme $\bigcup_{i\in I}T_i$. In particular, the $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal W$ are open immersions and their pullbacks form an open covering of every scheme mapping to $\mathcal W$. The empty family gives the empty open substack.

source.place: Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks), set-sizedness from the inclusion-preserving bijection with open subsets; Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks), statement and proof, including the cartesian scheme-pullback diagrams.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:P\to\mathcal X$ and put $R=P\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with projections $s,t$. By [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], pullback identifies open substacks, up to equivalence over $\mathcal X$, with the open subschemes $V\subseteq P$ satisfying $s^{-1}V=t^{-1}V$. Open subschemes of the fixed scheme $P$ are specified by open subsets of its underlying set. Thus the invariant ones form a subset of its power set, a set in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. The inverse of the cited bijection selects one representative for each invariant open, giving the required set of representatives.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open case and factorization criterion; Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks); Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks).

proof.text: For the given set-indexed family put $V_i=P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_i$. The cited correspondence gives $s^{-1}V_i=t^{-1}V_i$. Define the open subscheme $V\subseteq P$ by the ordinary union $\bigcup_i|V_i|$. Then $s^{-1}V=\bigcup_i s^{-1}V_i=\bigcup_i t^{-1}V_i=t^{-1}V$: each equality is the identity that membership in an inverse image of a union means membership in one inverse image. The equalities of open subspaces of $R$ can be checked after every scheme chart, where they are these same equalities of open subsets. Hence $V$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent].

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open case and factorization criterion; Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks); Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] to $V$ to obtain an open substack $\mathcal W$ with $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W=V$. Take its strictly full representative, by including all objects isomorphic to its objects; this changes neither the fibre products nor its equivalence class. This open substack is algebraic, as can also be checked directly: it is a stack because it is a substack; for any scheme maps $T,U\to\mathcal W$, full faithfulness identifies $T\times_{\mathcal W}U$ with $T\times_{\mathcal X}U$, so its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. The scheme $V$ maps to $\mathcal W$. For any scheme map $T\to\mathcal W$, the equality $V=P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$ identifies $T\times_{\mathcal W}V\to T$ with $T\times_{\mathcal X}P\to T$. The identification sends a pair with its comparison isomorphism to the same pair over $\mathcal X$; full faithfulness of $\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$ gives its inverse. The latter projection is smooth and surjective by the final assertion of [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent]. Thus $V\to\mathcal W$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas. The fibre-product identifications follow directly from the triples and comparison isomorphisms of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The same defining diagonal and atlas checks apply to each given open substack $\mathcal X_i$ and to every comparison open $\mathcal Z$: replace $V$ by its open atlas pullback. Thus these substacks are algebraic before invoking the factorization criterion in the next step.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open case and factorization criterion; Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks); Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks).

proof.text: The factorization criterion in [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], applied to $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$, shows that it factors through $\mathcal W$, since its atlas pullback $V_i\to P$ factors through $V$. For any other open substack $\mathcal Z$ containing every $\mathcal X_i$, let $Z=P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z$. Then $V_i\subseteq Z$ for every $i$, so $V\subseteq Z$. Apply the same factorization criterion with $\mathcal Y=\mathcal W$: its atlas pullback $V\to P$ factors through $Z$, hence $\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$ factors through $\mathcal Z$. For each object $x$ of the source substack over a scheme $T$, a factorization over $\mathcal X$ gives an object of the target substack isomorphic to $x$ in $\mathcal X(T)$. Strict fullness puts $x$ itself in the target substack; fullness includes every arrow between such objects. Thus these factorizations express containment of the specified substacks. This proves the least-upper-bound property.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open case and factorization criterion; Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks); Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks).

proof.text: Fix a scheme map $T\to\mathcal X$. Write $W_T=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$, $T_i=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_i$, and $Q=T\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with $q:Q\to T$ and $b:Q\to P$. These are open subschemes $W_T,T_i\subseteq T$, and $q$ is surjective by [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent]. The definition of 2-fibre products in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives $q^{-1}W_T=b^{-1}V$ and $q^{-1}T_i=b^{-1}V_i$. Since $V=\bigcup_iV_i$, ordinary inverse-image identities, checked on scheme charts of $Q$, give $q^{-1}W_T=\bigcup_iq^{-1}T_i=q^{-1}(\bigcup_iT_i)$. For each point $t\in T$, choose $z\in Q$ above it, using the stated surjectivity. The displayed equality says $t\in W_T$ if and only if $z\in q^{-1}W_T$, if and only if $z\in q^{-1}T_i$ for some $i$, if and only if $t\in T_i$ for some $i$. Thus the open subsets, and hence their corresponding open subschemes of $T$, are equal: $W_T=\bigcup_iT_i$. All identifications are over $T$, so this is the asserted scheme-pullback identification.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open case and factorization criterion; Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks); Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks).

proof.text: For a scheme $T\to\mathcal W$, the preceding equality says that the open subschemes $T\times_{\mathcal W}\mathcal X_i=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_i$ cover $T$; the identification follows from full faithfulness and the fibre-product definition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Consequently every $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal W$ is an open immersion and these immersions give exactly the covering asserted in the statement. If $I$ is empty, the preceding calculation says $W_T=\varnothing$ for every $T\to\mathcal X$. An object of $\mathcal W(T)$ would supply a section of $W_T\to T$, impossible unless $T$ is empty; over the empty scheme the empty etale covering has exactly one descent datum, effectiveness supplies an object, and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms supplies a unique arrow between any two objects. Thus the fibre there is equivalent to the terminal groupoid. Hence $\mathcal W$ is the empty open substack, including its required value over the empty scheme.
